title: Prompt Injection
summary: Crafted prompts cause the LLM to behave in ways unintended by the system designer — bypassing safety policies, leaking system prompts, or executing attacker-controlled instructions that arrived as data. Indirect prompt injection propagates via tool outputs the model ingests.
tool_risk_hints: tools that fetch untrusted URLs into context (web_fetch, read_webpage)
tools that read user-uploaded files without sanitization
MCP servers exposing arbitrary prompt/context manipulation
shell tools invoked with user-supplied arguments that end up in stdout

title: Sensitive Information Disclosure
summary: The LLM reveals credentials, PII, internal system prompts, training data, or proprietary business logic through its outputs — either in the direct response or leaked through tool arguments.
tool_risk_hints: file-read tools with access to credential paths (.ssh, .aws, .env)
shell commands that echo environment variables
database tools without row-level authorization
tools that serialize full user records into model context

title: Supply Chain
summary: Malicious dependencies, untrusted pre-trained models, plugins, or datasets introduce vulnerabilities into the LLM system.
tool_risk_hints: package install tools (pip, npm, cargo, gem) executed during agent runs
tools that fetch and run remote scripts (curl|sh patterns)
MCP server installation / auto-enablement without review

title: Data and Model Poisoning
summary: Training data, fine-tuning data, or retrieval corpora are manipulated to introduce back-doored behavior, biased outputs, or toxic content.
tool_risk_hints: tools that write into RAG knowledge bases without review
tools that modify embedding stores
tools that fetch and persist untrusted documents

title: Improper Output Handling
summary: Downstream systems trust LLM output without validation, enabling XSS, SQL injection, SSRF, or remote code execution when the model emits code, URLs, or structured data.
tool_risk_hints: SQL execution tools that take the model's raw string
HTTP clients issuing arbitrary outbound requests
shell/exec tools that run the model's command verbatim

title: Excessive Agency
summary: The agent has more tools, permissions, or autonomy than the task requires, enabling unintended destructive actions when prompts, inputs, or outputs go wrong.
tool_risk_hints: delete / drop / destroy tools exposed without a confirmation gate
production-write tools available in dev/test agent sessions
privilege-escalation tools (sudo, doas) reachable by the agent

title: System Prompt Leakage
summary: The system prompt is exposed to users or attackers, revealing business logic, policy, credentials embedded in prompts, or tool-routing hints that aid future attacks.
tool_risk_hints: debug / introspection tools that echo the system prompt
tools that serialize the full chat transcript

title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
summary: RAG pipelines are manipulated via poisoned vector stores, embedding inversions, or retrieval of attacker-controlled chunks that alter model behavior.
tool_risk_hints: tools that bulk-ingest untrusted text into vector stores
retrieval tools without source attribution or tenant filtering

title: Misinformation
summary: The model emits confidently-stated but incorrect information, causing downstream decisions to rely on hallucinated data — especially dangerous in tool-enabled agents that take action on that output.
tool_risk_hints: tools that act on LLM-generated identifiers (IDs, emails, URLs) without validation
tools that commit transactions based on unverified model claims

title: Unbounded Consumption
summary: Tool-enabled agents make unlimited API calls, incur runaway costs, exfiltrate large volumes of data, or trigger DoS on downstream systems.
tool_risk_hints: HTTP tools invoked in loops without rate limit
file-read tools that walk unbounded directory trees
database tools issuing SELECT * without limits

title: External Harms
summary: Attackers use an ML-enabled agent to cause harms outside the target system — e.g. spamming third parties, sending phishing, or launching network attacks against external infrastructure.
tool_risk_hints: email / messaging tools (send_email, slack_post, sms_send)
HTTP tools able to target arbitrary external URLs
tools that trigger outbound notifications to user-controlled addresses

title: Exfiltration via ML Inference API
summary: Adversaries abuse LLM outputs or tool-invocation side effects to move sensitive data out of the target environment through the inference / tool pipeline.
tool_risk_hints: tools that upload files to external services
DNS lookup / network tools that can encode data into hostnames
webhook / outbound HTTP tools

title: LLM Prompt Injection
summary: MITRE's complement to OWASP LLM01 — adversaries craft user prompts or poisoned tool outputs that redirect the model's behavior.
tool_risk_hints: tools that ingest untrusted content (web pages, emails, files)
retrieval tools without provenance tagging

title: LLM Plugin Compromise
summary: A compromised or malicious plugin / tool / MCP server is invoked by the agent, executing attacker-controlled code or exfiltrating data.
tool_risk_hints: tools served by third-party MCP servers without attestation
plugins with overly broad OAuth scopes
tool handlers that execute plugin-provided shell fragments

title: LLM Jailbreak
summary: Adversary bypasses safety policies baked into the model or system prompt, enabling tool invocations or outputs the deployer intended to forbid.
tool_risk_hints: high-risk destructive tools that rely on model-side refusal
tools gated only by system-prompt instructions, no server-side policy

title: OS Command Injection
summary: User-controlled data reaches a shell invocation without sanitization. In LLM agent contexts, this is triggered when the model emits shell commands built from attacker-supplied input.
tool_risk_hints: Bash / shell / exec tools with user-derived arguments
tools that concatenate strings into subprocess invocations

title: Path Traversal
summary: Relative paths (../) or absolute paths into sensitive directories bypass access controls on file-read/write tools.
tool_risk_hints: Read / Write / Edit tools with no path allow-list
file-upload tools that preserve attacker-supplied filenames

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
summary: Tools issuing HTTP requests to URLs derived from untrusted input can probe internal networks or cloud metadata endpoints.
tool_risk_hints: web_fetch / http_get tools without URL allow-list
tools that resolve user-supplied hostnames

title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
summary: Tools that deserialize pickle, YAML, or binary formats from attacker-controlled sources enable arbitrary code execution.
tool_risk_hints: tools that load Python pickle / Ruby Marshal / PHP serialize
MCP servers that accept serialized plugin state

title: SQL Injection
summary: The LLM emits or concatenates SQL text containing attacker-controlled data, reaching a database tool that executes it verbatim.
tool_risk_hints: database query tools accepting raw SQL strings
tools building queries from model output without parameterization

title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
summary: Tools that read or print credential files, or agent runs that embed secrets in tool arguments.
tool_risk_hints: file-read tools with access to .env / credentials
shell tools that echo KEY=VALUE env exports
